_read_me: The expected schema is declared outside the DDL that applies it.
This file exists because the schema job's check used to be TAUTOLOGICAL: it derived the
declaration from the very questdb-init.sql it had just applied, against a QuestDB that
starts empty on every run. Changing PARTITION BY DAY to MONTH in the DDL moved BOTH SIDES
of the comparison, and the job passed — measured against the real 8.2.3. The only outcome
that comparison could catch was 'the engine disagreed with the DDL', which is not what the
schema contract asks for.
With this declaration the axis changes: the job compares the ENGINE against what is WRITTEN
HERE. Changing the DDL without changing this file now FAILS — which is the point. Changing
partitionBy on a live table is an irreversible decision (PARTITION BY is immutable and
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is a silent success over a table born wrong), so it must cost a
deliberate edit in TWO files, with the pair visible in the diff.
HOW TO EDIT: did you change the DDL on purpose? Edit here too, in the same commit. A red
job is not an obstacle — it is the question 'did you decide this?' asked before the
partition exists.
SCOPE: only what is IMMUTABLE or structural per table: partitioning, WAL, dedup and the
UPSERT key columns. The COLUMN list is deliberately absent: a new column is
QuestDBStore.EnsureSchema's responsibility (probe-then-ALTER, on every boot), so freezing
it here would fail every legitimate addition.
Checked by .github/workflows/schema.yml against questdb/questdb:8.2.3.
